findings.result: 32 versus 16 requests for eight tasks in each block, with correct effects retained.

findings.observation: A 64-tool catalog can keep full schemas deferred.
findings.interpretation: A measured context/wire-footprint benefit supports the extensibility/per-call-context design. CPU and throughput changed direction between blocks, so a necessary performance sacrifice is not established.

findings.observation: Global overlap increased while short-task goodput did not scale proportionally.
findings.test: SRC-02 cap 1/4 crossed with 150/1500 ms independent effects
findings.result: Long-wait goodput improved about 2.52x in both paired blocks; short-wait improvements were about 1.16x/1.47x. Callback PIDs matched the Gateway inspector owner and were on its main thread.
findings.interpretation: The knob admits concurrent asynchronous runs; it does not create four JavaScript execution threads. The benefit grows when independent waiting can overlap.
unresolved: Unique residual short-task bottleneck; worker CPU versus main-thread bookkeeping; same-session ordering ablation.

findings.observation: Code plugin termination affected the Gateway while a tool-process termination did not.
findings.test: SRC-03 ordinary throw, explicit exit, callback identity and owned-file authority
findings.result: All four throw probes preserved the original Gateway owner and successful independent requests. Native plugin callbacks matched the Gateway PID/main thread; external MCP callbacks had different PIDs but the same UID and could read the same explicitly accessible canary.
findings.interpretation: Logical lifecycle scope and ordinary error conversion are not a process/OS permission boundary. Deep code extension and a shared termination/authority domain are structurally coupled; their overall net value is not scored.
unresolved: One native exit fast-poll was transitional: availability failed although immediate process polling still said live. The raw field is retained. A passive settlement observation was added for future runs.
Pure IPC overhead and net extension benefit are not isolated.
Every request in this experiment used a fresh session; source MCP runtime acquisition is session-keyed, so lifecycle costs also differ.

findings.observation: Session scope separated the working directory.
findings.test: SRC-04 relative lookup versus explicit owned sibling path under one SSH principal
findings.result: Relative canary lookup differed by scope; the explicit sibling read returned readable=true in all four arms.
findings.interpretation: Workspace identity and remote OS identity are different owners. This root-SSH deployment does not become an OS jail by changing scope; this is not a claim that OpenClaw promised hostile-tenant isolation or that Docker behaves the same.
unresolved: Independent OS-user/container backends and their isolation/resource costs.

findings.observation: Native tool-error previews replaced the synthetic token argument with ***.
findings.test: Existing SRC-03 error logs, followed by exact-source inspection; no new runtime intervention is claimed.
findings.result: The error adapter deliberately redacts previews; tools-mode defaults include credential-shaped JSON keys such as token.
findings.interpretation: Credential-protection policy intentionally limits raw argument visibility in this log surface. It can also mask a benign correlation value. This does not prove full privacy protection or missing data in every authorized trace/export surface.
unresolved: Blind diagnosis accuracy, public trace/export accessibility and adversarial secret leakage.

findings.observation: Path/ownership, worker-admission and redaction functions appeared in retained V8 sample stacks.
findings.result: Source guards canonicalize aliases, enforce current ownership/maintenance access, and already contain freshness/heartbeat-conditioned read caching.
findings.interpretation: These are real consistency/privacy responsibilities, but sparse samples do not establish dominant cost or prove that removing a guard is a valid optimization.
findings.next_discriminating_test: Use owned state only: compare stable-path/cache behavior with controlled alias or owner-lock replacement, preserving task correctness and recording refusals. Any guard bypass must be a separately labeled private counterfactual, not the product baseline.
